name: Fetch user-supplied URLs securely
query: Users can paste any website URL into my plugin's settings page, and the plugin fetches that URL to import content into posts. Right now the admin form handler does wp_remote_get($_POST['url']) and it works, but I want the import wired up properly before we ship it.
expected_behavior: Locate the outbound HTTP request and classify the URL as untrusted because it comes from $_POST['url'] user input.
Read the URL with esc_url_raw( wp_unslash( $_POST['url'] ) ) before any validation.

Parse the host with wp_parse_url( $url, PHP_URL_HOST ) and reject the request unless the host is in an explicit allowlist (in_array on the lowercased host), excluding localhost, link-local, and metadata addresses.
Run wp_http_validate_url( $url ) as an additional guard so only http/https URLs pass and private/loopback ranges are blocked.
Replace wp_remote_get() with wp_safe_remote_get() so the URL and every redirect target are validated against internal addresses.
Check is_wp_error( $response ) before reading the response and log failures without exposing internal network details.
Accept only response status codes supported by the import format, with timeout, redirect, and response-size limits before processing the body.
Retrieve the content with wp_remote_retrieve_body( $response ) and treat the body as untrusted input before output or storage.
success_criteria: wp_remote_get() on the user-supplied URL is replaced with wp_safe_remote_get().
The host is compared against an explicit allowlist before the request, excluding localhost, 169.254.169.254, and other internal or metadata addresses.
Only supported HTTP(S) targets and redirect destinations are reachable; domain policy and SSRF validation cannot be bypassed through redirects.
is_wp_error() is checked before any part of the response is read.
wp_remote_retrieve_response_code() validates the response code (2xx) before the body is used.
The fetched body is escaped or sanitized before output or storage.
